description: Visual semantics are disjoint axes; color conveys outcome only when paired with a text label.

mapping.root_rule: one accountable repair owner per confirmed causal root

repository_protection.channel: card_border + explicit status text + scoped shield

protected.label: PROTECTED
protected.meaning: effective branch protection reported (independent merge approval not claimed)

ruleset_configuration.channel: gold configuration count + action badge + expanded native rule names
ruleset_configuration.guard: Count of rules is NOT the number of passing CI checks.

workflow_family.channel: outlined badge with text family code, independent from execution outcome

workflow_repetition.channel: expandable grouped cohort with preserved native run links
workflow_repetition.guard: Roll-up affects presentation only; never removes runs from numerator/denominator.

measurement_granularity.guard: Execution depth and repeated evidence describe granularity; they do not increase independent process sample size.

constraints: No operational meaning assigned to a filled purple brand card.
Colors cannot replace named role, numbered phase or proof level.
No identical HEX color for two native execution outcomes.
Conditional green YES does not signify actual present admission.
Forward DAG is acyclic; feedback/feedforward visualized in independent overlay.
The rendered UI must retain text state labels for accessibility and disambiguation.
Repository test/coverage proof and physical plant safety colors are separate domains.
Branch protected=true is not equivalent to admission PASS; show mandatory CI and review separately.
Configuration colors, execution colors, and ownership/phase markings must not be used as interchangeable evidence.
Workflow roll-ups retain native individual run IDs and SHA links for audit.
Telemetry family/granularity styling must not reuse native outcome colors as a semantic status code.
Workflow/job/step/test/root counts are nested or repeated evidence unless an independent-cycle producer proves otherwise.
